S6-01 creates one immutable, tenant/Site-scoped Action identity from a reviewed persisted `FindingRevision` under the canonical Finding route. It pins the originating revision, selected assessment and accepted-evidence/configuration basis; a later Finding revision does not silently rewrite that origin. A Finding may have several Actions, but each accepted recommendation creates or idempotently returns one Action for its server-defined command key. The recommendation is a bounded proposed reserve-SOC policy trial with explicit purpose, limitation and source Finding; it is not a measured saving or verified outcome. The Action detail root is `/sites/{site}/actions/{action_id}` with stable child routes and exact `event_id` selection, and Site/Finding back-links. S6-01 may navigate from a known Finding or Action ID before the separate S6-03 Site ActionIndex exists. Hidden unsupported tabs must not masquerade as empty delivered views.

Action state is derived from an append-only, server-ordered `ActionEvent` ledger. Record stable event ID, Action and Site, event type, `occurred_at`, server `recorded_at`, idempotency key, actor kind/ID, source channel, authorization basis and triggering command/job or content revision. Idempotent identical retries return the event; conflicting reuse and cross-Site references fail. Historical reads select a recorded cutoff and then `(recorded_at,id)` order; a backdated `occurred_at` is displayed as such but never rewrites the audit order. `PROPOSED`/`ACCEPTED`, application `PENDING`/`APPLIED`/`FAILED`, and later verification status are separate dimensions. Acceptance does not assert application; an applied change or completed work does not assert benefit. A failed application preserves its attempt, error and retry relation without an effective-policy claim. No human author, approval or attestation is inferred from a gateway credential, client field, local OS user or SYSTEM fixture. Under the existing `A-actor-identity` rule, human writes need a verified operator principal; otherwise only a clearly labelled, server-authorized SYSTEM demonstration command with stable service/job provenance is allowed, or the write stays unavailable.

The supported S6-01 change is a controlled reserve-SOC edit through S1 Foundation publish, producing a new immutable effective `FoundationRevision` and an immutable change artifact that links Action, accepted recommendation, authorized command, old/new revision IDs, exact field/value/unit, validity and recorded time, and the application event. Validate the expected old revision and Site scope under the publish lock; reject stale, unauthorized or invalid edits and record a failed attempt without claiming the new setting took effect. `APPLIED` requires confirmation of the persisted new effective revision; an ActionEvent alone is insufficient. The old basis and every event/change revision remain addressable after reload. Do not mutate a Lab-only override or rewrite accepted evidence. S6-01's Execution/History and applied `changes:1#a` show policy activity with event and configuration provenance, including pending/failed cases; they do not show an effect verdict.

S6-02 owns the separate immutable `VerificationPlanRevision` and later `VerificationOutcome`. A plan pins this Action, the applied-change event and new Foundation revision, a pre-change baseline assessment/evidence basis, target, service/reserve guardrails, required coverage and later-window selection rule before evaluation. Use separate baseline and later Lab runs under their respective fixed effective Foundation revisions; commit their public reports through the ordinary gateway and central acceptance. Evaluate a closed later accepted window against the frozen plan and baseline, with exact analytic/evidence IDs. Missing or conflicting evidence yields `INCONCLUSIVE`; failed guardrail prevents `VERIFIED` even if the target improves; later results append/supersede without rewriting prior outcomes. Plan/evidence/verification child routes preserve exact plan and outcome IDs. `A-S6-verification` remains open for the full comparison rule; this lifecycle decision does not resolve it. S6-03 alone owns the Site-scoped ActionIndex/list and its watermarked empty/positive states; `A-action-index` remains open. ## Window and frozen plan

Use `reserve-trial-verification-1`, version 1. The Action must be APPLIED with a committed change artifact. Freeze an immutable VerificationPlanRevision before the later run or its first accepted report. It pins Action, origin FindingRevision, applied event, old and new FoundationRevision, baseline selected S3 assessment/run and accepted evidence IDs, model/cohort/clock basis, target, guardrails, coverage rule and explicit two-window selection. A new plan revision can replace a pending plan only before later evidence is accepted; after that, a new attempt needs a new plan revision and later window. Never edit a plan or silently substitute a newer Finding/assessment.

The baseline is a closed, assessed, half-open 60-minute UTC window wholly before the applied revision's `effective_from`, under the old covering FoundationRevision. The later window is another closed, half-open 60-minute UTC window wholly at or after that effective time, under the new covering revision. Neither window may straddle a policy change. The plan fixes their UTC bounds before the later run; both have the same duration and clock hour, and cite comparable Site, asset, dispatch model version, signal roles and cohort rule. Differences in load/PV or other operating conditions are displayed as limitations; if they prevent a like-for-like comparison under the plan's predeclared comparable-input bands, return INCONCLUSIVE. This is an observed policy-trial comparison, not a causal saving. The S3 `CANDIDATE_AVOIDABLE` duration in minutes from the selected 60-minute dispatch assessment is the target metric; do not substitute all generator run time, a money amount or a Finding count. Baseline must have positive supported Candidate minutes. Version 1 target is at least a 25% reduction in Candidate minutes (`later <= 0.75 * baseline`), with the exact integer/decimal comparison and bounds stored in the plan. Both windows require final S3 selection and complete S4 episode reassessment for the selected Finding. A later `NO_LONGER_SUPPORTED` FindingRevision can corroborate but cannot replace the numeric window comparison.

Minimum coverage is every required five-minute slot in both windows for generator state/power, load, PV, battery SOC and effective reserve; require the dispatch capability inputs needed for Candidate classification, accepted clock/cohort proof and no material rejected/overlapping/contradictory span. A missing slot or required role is insufficient, even if the remaining slots show improvement. Service guardrail requires accepted requested and delivered critical-load power for every slot, or a separately reviewed equivalent service-availability signal; compare unserved critical energy over both windows and require later <= baseline. Reserve guardrail requires accepted SOC and time-valid reserve throughout, with zero post-change minutes below the effective reserve and no increase over baseline. Terminal SOC at identical horizon must be at least baseline terminal SOC after a predeclared comparable initial-SOC band; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE. A service or reserve limit that cannot be measured remains UNKNOWN, never pass. The Planner must version the five-minute publication profile and readiness/missing-input messages for both Lab and real-Site onboarding; no private simulator state fills public gaps.

## Verdict, history and hold

Only `VERIFIED`, `INEFFECTIVE`, `INCONCLUSIVE` are outcome values. Before a closed, settled later window, display `PENDING` as verification state, not an outcome. On a fully assessable pair, `VERIFIED` requires the target and every guardrail to pass. `INEFFECTIVE` means the target fails or any measured guardrail fails. Store `GUARDRAIL_FAIL` as a reason with each failed metric, value, threshold and evidence IDs; it is not a fourth outcome. If a required target, guardrail, source designation, comparability or selection is unknown/ambiguous, return `INCONCLUSIVE`, even when another measured metric failed; retain the known failure as a finding within the outcome, never imply success. A positive verdict requires one coherent stored source designation for each window (`REGISTERED_SIMULATION` for the demo, or `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION` for an explicitly authored case) and a compatible pair declared in the plan. `MIXED`, `UNKNOWN`, broken links, or crossing source classes fail closed to INCONCLUSIVE. No real-source positive verdict until separately attested real provenance exists. Label simulated/authored results and make no realized-saving claim.

Late accepted readings, changed clock attestation, source classification, or pending/failed S3 or S4 recomputation immediately mark the latest verdict `REASSESSMENT_PENDING` (a read state, not a fourth outcome) and withdraw its current Verified/Resolved presentation. Keep the old outcome addressable as historical. Once settled, append a new immutable outcome referencing exact selected assessment, FindingRevision, accepted SourceEnvelope IDs/digests, provenance resolution, plan and comparison values; supersede by link, never UPDATE. Identical evaluation retries return the same outcome; a changed basis yields a new outcome. Exact plan/outcome ID and recorded cutoff reads remain stable. A later recurring Finding is a new episode/link, not a rewrite of the prior outcome or proof that the old trial never happened.

Application and verification states remain separate. An APPLIED Action is unresolved while PENDING, REASSESSMENT_PENDING or INCONCLUSIVE. A final current VERIFIED or INEFFECTIVE outcome appends a `RESOLVED` ActionEvent (with outcome ID, plan ID and result) and closes that trial for the prior-Action acceptance guard; INEFFECTIVE means the trial is resolved as unsuccessful, not the Finding repaired. A new reserve trial still needs a fresh current supported FindingRevision and current Foundation basis. A pending or failed application has no verification plan and keeps the hold; a future explicit cancellation/abandonment contract is outside S6-02. If late evidence invalidates the final basis, append a `RESOLUTION_WITHDRAWN` event, restore the hold under the same Site/Finding/asset/field/rule serialization used by accept, and block a new accept while reassessment is pending. If a subsequent Action already exists, do not delete it; flag the overlap and prevent another acceptance until reviewed. The guard and current outcome must be checked atomically, not from a stale UI projection.

The evaluation is system-computed from accepted public evidence. A server-authorized SYSTEM demonstration command may freeze the plan, request evaluation or append the resolution event, with stable service/job and fixture provenance; it cannot supply a verdict or metric value. No gateway credential, client text or local user is a human author. Show the SYSTEM demonstration label. Each plan, evaluation request, outcome and ActionEvent is append-only with server recorded time and idempotency key; retries and exact-history selectors follow S6-01's recorded-order rule.

## Demo and delivery split

`I-sim-verification-cases` produces two separate fixed-policy Lab runs, old then new Foundation, through registered gateway and ordinary S2 acceptance. A replayable manifest cites public run/batch/envelope IDs, plan and expected selected S3/S4 revisions; private oracle stays in Lab. Include a complete target-and-guardrails pass, a complete target pass with a measured reserve or service guardrail failure (`INEFFECTIVE`, `GUARDRAIL_FAIL`), and missing service/terminal or contradictory/late evidence (`INCONCLUSIVE`, then reassessment and an appended settled result). Include a target miss, closed-window zero-finding basis and prior-Action hold/release proof. The examples say simulated policy trial and no causal or savings claim.

Build non-UI first: immutable plan/outcome persistence and Action events, rule evaluator, exact read APIs, source and pending-work gates, fixtures, replay/idempotency/race tests. Then UI: Recommendation plan/evidence, Action Plan/Evidence/Verification, `changes:1#b` and `changes:2`, with exact IDs, activity separate from effect, missing/pending/fail states at desktop and 390 px. S6-02 owner walkthrough remains required. S6-03 Site ActionIndex is independent.

frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp.md-43-SQLite in WAL mode contains gateway identity/configuration, mapping snapshots, local monotonic sequence allocation per stable source stream, append-only envelope outbox, upload batches/acknowledgements and compact health counters. Write envelope and sequence in one transaction before upload. Preserve bytes and IDs across restarts, backoff with jitter, retry identical batch bytes, and delete/compact only after the server confirms each envelope's accepted/duplicate/rejected/conflict outcome and the acknowledgement is durable locally. Rejected/conflicting messages move to an inspectable dead-letter state; a whole-batch refusal retains the batch for operator repair. Ordering is by source time plus sequence for analysis, never by arrival order; late records trigger recomputation of affected periods. A sequence gap is a source-health signal, not fabricated telemetry. Expose last device contact, queue age/depth, disk pressure, clock offset, last successful upload and mapping errors locally and centrally. Limit disk use with alerts and explicit retention policy; do not silently drop unacknowledged evidence.

frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md-179-3. **Decide records.** In one Postgres transaction, lock batch row; for each unprocessed ordinal parse strict envelope, verify identity/sequence and referenced mapping/Foundation validity at `source_time`, normalize with the registered as-accepted conversion, and insert acceptance or rejection plus disposition. Unique message key arbitrates concurrent duplicate deliveries. Equal digest is `DUPLICATE`; changed digest is `CONFLICT` and points to first accepted evidence. Update watermark and create/coalesce recompute jobs in the same commit. Chunk a large batch into short committed transactions; receipt exposes `IN_PROGRESS` until all ordinals are durable. A client retries the same batch/bytes and resumes from the persisted watermark. Return a terminal receipt only after all decisions commit.
frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md-180-4. **Assess.** Worker leases dirty site/domain/window jobs, selects accepted evidence by source time plus interval overlap at a declared knowledge cutoff, resolves the exact public configuration, builds `AnalyticInputSet`, and runs the versioned pure analytic. In one commit insert `AnalyticRun`, immutable assessment/finding/consequence revisions when basis changed, update projections and mark job done. Retry of same input hash is a no-op. Late or out-of-order evidence recomputes the affected and neighboring continuity window; it never mutates old revisions. Model deployment schedules explicit re-evaluation of supported windows.
frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md:181:5. **Verify.** ActionEvent records work. After a later closed window exists, evaluate the frozen plan against accepted evidence, target and each guardrail. Missing coverage is `INCONCLUSIVE`; worsening service prevents `VERIFIED` even if cost falls. Link outcome to exact analytic run/evidence and surface any later superseding outcome.
frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md-182-
frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md-183-**Initial API contract:** `POST /api/ingestion/batches` returns terminal `200` receipt or `202 IN_PROGRESS` receipt; `GET /api/ingestion/batches/{id}` returns the same durable state. `409` is reserved for same batch ID/different bytes or registered identity conflict, `422` for malformed contract, `401/403` for authentication/authorization. Normal reads use `GET /api/sites/{id}/evidence`, `/evidence/records/{id}`, `/overview`, `/performance/{view}`, `/findings/{id}` with `from`, `to` and optional `revision_id`; list reads paginate by stable `(source_time,id)` or `(created_at,id)` cursor. All responses include scope/window, revision IDs, evidence coverage and projection watermark. The UI treats a lagging projection as pending, not healthy. Lab Commit calls this same HTTP boundary with a registered simulated gateway; no privileged product-write endpoint exists.
--
frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md-185-**Gateway diagnostic API:** `POST /api/gateways/{gateway_id}/diagnostics` authenticates the registered gateway/site, checks `GatewayDiagnosticsV1` identity/hash and inserts `gateway_diagnostic` with server `received_at`; an identical retry returns the existing row. `409` refuses identity reuse with different bytes, `422` malformed fields, and `401/403` wrong credential/scope. `GET /api/sites/{id}/gateway-health` returns last server contact, declared cadence, source-contact observations, queue age/depth, disk pressure, clock offset and an explicit `CURRENT|STALE|UNKNOWN` status with diagnostic ID and receive time. It makes no claim that the device or asset itself is healthy. S2-01c publishes locally; S2-02 owns central storage and read API; S7 composes the Site Health claim.

frontend/docs/architecture/production-shaped-mvp-technical-design.md:187:**Demo-to-Postgres cutover:** create Tenant/Site/Gateway/Source registrations from existing Site records, import immutable Foundation and mapping versions, then replay sealed committed batch bytes through the new ingestion service using the legacy parsers. Preserve original batch/message IDs, envelope text, source times and mode; assign new database UUIDs only to internal rows. Compare accepted/rejected/conflict counts and representative evidence/dispatch claims against the file-backed baseline. Keep `var/sites`, Lab runs, stages and committed artifacts untouched and read-only during verification. Switch product reads to Postgres only after the comparison passes; new Lab Commit posts the V2 batch/receipt path. Do not import private world trajectories into the product database. Choose (c): show the earlier Action and hold a repeat trial while it is unresolved. +Decision: `D-2026-10-16-s6-verification`. This closes the architecture gate only. S6-02 remains an outline, implementation and owner visual acceptance remain open. This ruling applies `D-2026-10-14-action-lifecycle-and-policy-application` (including its S6-02 paragraph), `D-2026-10-15-s601-action-store-and-ui` and `D-2026-10-15-s601-reopen`.
 
 ## Window and frozen plan
 
 Use `reserve-trial-verification-1`, version 1. The Action must be APPLIED with a committed change artifact. Freeze an immutable VerificationPlanRevision before the later run or its first accepted report. It pins Action, origin FindingRevision, applied event, old and new FoundationRevision, baseline selected S3 assessment/run and accepted evidence IDs, model/cohort/clock basis, target, guardrails, coverage rule and explicit two-window selection. A new plan revision can replace a pending plan only before later evidence is accepted; after that, a new attempt needs a new plan revision and later window. Never edit a plan or silently substitute a newer Finding/assessment.
 
-The baseline is a closed, assessed, half-open 60-minute UTC window wholly before the applied revision's `effective_from`, under the old covering FoundationRevision. The later window is another closed, half-open 60-minute UTC window wholly at or after that effective time, under the new covering revision. Neither window may straddle a policy change. The plan fixes their UTC bounds before the later run; both have the same duration and clock hour, and cite comparable Site, asset, dispatch model version, signal roles and cohort rule. Differences in load/PV or other operating conditions are displayed as limitations; if they prevent a like-for-like comparison under the plan's predeclared comparable-input bands, return INCONCLUSIVE. This is an observed policy-trial comparison, not a causal saving. The S3 `CANDIDATE_AVOIDABLE` duration in minutes from the selected 60-minute dispatch assessment is the target metric; do not substitute all generator run time, a money amount or a Finding count. Baseline must have positive supported Candidate minutes. Version 1 target is at least a 25% reduction in Candidate minutes (`later <= 0.75 * baseline`), with the exact integer/decimal comparison and bounds stored in the plan. Both windows require final S3 selection and complete S4 episode reassessment for the selected Finding. A later `NO_LONGER_SUPPORTED` FindingRevision can corroborate but cannot replace the numeric window comparison.

A segment crossing a bound contributes only its overlap; indeterminate or open-bound segment time intersecting the window makes the target INCONCLUSIVE. A later `NO_LONGER_SUPPORTED` FindingRevision can corroborate but cannot replace the numeric window comparison. A different covering FoundationRevision for either window, including a backdated publication, makes the current result REASSESSMENT_PENDING while recomputation runs, then INCONCLUSIVE unless a new comparable plan is frozen.
 
-Minimum coverage is every required five-minute slot in both windows for generator state/power, load, PV, battery SOC and effective reserve; require the dispatch capability inputs needed for Candidate classification, accepted clock/cohort proof and no material rejected/overlapping/contradictory span. A missing slot or required role is insufficient, even if the remaining slots show improvement. Service guardrail requires accepted requested and delivered critical-load power for every slot, or a separately reviewed equivalent service-availability signal; compare unserved critical energy over both windows and require later <= baseline. Reserve guardrail requires accepted SOC and time-valid reserve throughout, with zero post-change minutes below the effective reserve and no increase over baseline. Terminal SOC at identical horizon must be at least baseline terminal SOC after a predeclared comparable initial-SOC band; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE. A service or reserve limit that cannot be measured remains UNKNOWN, never pass. The Planner must version the five-minute publication profile and readiness/missing-input messages for both Lab and real-Site onboarding; no private simulator state fills public gaps.

 ## Verdict, history and hold
 
-Only `VERIFIED`, `INEFFECTIVE`, `INCONCLUSIVE` are outcome values. Before a closed, settled later window, display `PENDING` as verification state, not an outcome. On a fully assessable pair, `VERIFIED` requires the target and every guardrail to pass. `INEFFECTIVE` means the target fails or any measured guardrail fails. Store `GUARDRAIL_FAIL` as a reason with each failed metric, value, threshold and evidence IDs; it is not a fourth outcome. If a required target, guardrail, source designation, comparability or selection is unknown/ambiguous, return `INCONCLUSIVE`, even when another measured metric failed; retain the known failure as a finding within the outcome, never imply success. A positive verdict requires one coherent stored source designation for each window (`REGISTERED_SIMULATION` for the demo, or `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION` for an explicitly authored case) and a compatible pair declared in the plan. `MIXED`, `UNKNOWN`, broken links, or crossing source classes fail closed to INCONCLUSIVE. No real-source positive verdict until separately attested real provenance exists. Label simulated/authored results and make no realized-saving claim.
+Only `VERIFIED`, `INEFFECTIVE`, `INCONCLUSIVE` are outcome values. Before a closed, settled later window, display `PENDING` as verification state, not an outcome. On a fully assessable pair, `VERIFIED` requires the target and every guardrail to pass. `INEFFECTIVE` means the target fails or any measured guardrail fails. Store `GUARDRAIL_FAIL` as a reason with each failed metric, value, threshold and evidence IDs; it is not a fourth outcome. If a required target, guardrail, source designation, comparability or selection is unknown/ambiguous, return `INCONCLUSIVE`, even when another measured metric failed; retain the known failure as a finding within the outcome, never imply success. Resolve stored provenance separately for each window, never over their union. A positive verdict requires one coherent source designation per window (`REGISTERED_SIMULATION` for the demo, or `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION` for an explicitly authored case). The plan's compatible-pair rule requires the same source class and registered scenario/profile lineage, distinct run identity digests and intact links; pin both resolutions and digests in the outcome. `MIXED`, `UNKNOWN`, broken links, or crossing source classes fail closed to INCONCLUSIVE. No real-source positive verdict until separately attested real provenance exists. Label simulated/authored results and make no realized-saving claim.
 
 Late accepted readings, changed clock attestation, source classification, or pending/failed S3 or S4 recomputation immediately mark the latest verdict `REASSESSMENT_PENDING` (a read state, not a fourth outcome) and withdraw its current Verified/Resolved presentation. Keep the old outcome addressable as historical. Once settled, append a new immutable outcome referencing exact selected assessment, FindingRevision, accepted SourceEnvelope IDs/digests, provenance resolution, plan and comparison values; supersede by link, never UPDATE. Identical evaluation retries return the same outcome; a changed basis yields a new outcome. Exact plan/outcome ID and recorded cutoff reads remain stable. A later recurring Finding is a new episode/link, not a rewrite of the prior outcome or proof that the old trial never happened.
 
-Application and verification states remain separate. An APPLIED Action is unresolved while PENDING, REASSESSMENT_PENDING or INCONCLUSIVE. A final current VERIFIED or INEFFECTIVE outcome appends a `RESOLVED` ActionEvent (with outcome ID, plan ID and result) and closes that trial for the prior-Action acceptance guard; INEFFECTIVE means the trial is resolved as unsuccessful, not the Finding repaired. A new reserve trial still needs a fresh current supported FindingRevision and current Foundation basis. A pending or failed application has no verification plan and keeps the hold; a future explicit cancellation/abandonment contract is outside S6-02. If late evidence invalidates the final basis, append a `RESOLUTION_WITHDRAWN` event, restore the hold under the same Site/Finding/asset/field/rule serialization used by accept, and block a new accept while reassessment is pending. If a subsequent Action already exists, do not delete it; flag the overlap and prevent another acceptance until reviewed. The guard and current outcome must be checked atomically, not from a stale UI projection.

-The evaluation is system-computed from accepted public evidence. A server-authorized SYSTEM demonstration command may freeze the plan, request evaluation or append the resolution event, with stable service/job and fixture provenance; it cannot supply a verdict or metric value. No gateway credential, client text or local user is a human author. Show the SYSTEM demonstration label.  ## Demo and delivery split

Include a complete target-and-guardrails pass, a complete target pass with a measured reserve or service guardrail failure (`INEFFECTIVE`, `GUARDRAIL_FAIL`), and missing service/terminal or contradictory/late evidence (`INCONCLUSIVE`, then reassessment and an appended settled result). Include a target miss, closed-window zero-finding basis and prior-Action hold/release proof. The examples say simulated policy trial and no causal or savings claim.

On a fully assessable pair, `VERIFIED` requires the target and every guardrail to pass. `INEFFECTIVE` means the target fails or any measured guardrail fails. Store `GUARDRAIL_FAIL` as a reason with each failed metric, value, threshold and evidence IDs; it is not a fourth outcome. If a required target, guardrail, source designation, comparability or selection is unknown/ambiguous, return `INCONCLUSIVE`, even when another measured metric failed; retain the known failure as a finding within the outcome, never imply success. A positive verdict requires one coherent stored source designation for each window (`REGISTERED_SIMULATION` for the demo, or `AUTHORED_DEMONSTRATION` for an explicitly authored case) and a compatible pair declared in the plan. `MIXED`, `UNKNOWN`, broken links, or crossing source classes fail closed to INCONCLUSIVE. No real-source positive verdict until separately attested real provenance exists. Label simulated/authored results and make no realized-saving claim.
